scope: GF8 legacy-high pure-AVX2 K=2,R=1 ordinary one-shot encode at 64, 256, and 1024 bytes
hypothesis: A straight-line integer-range success proof could preserve the full overlap contract while avoiding the mature K2/R1 validator's general range construction on valid public calls.

execution.ratio_orientation: control time divided by candidate time; above one favors the candidate

candidates.name: separate public-entry success helper
candidates.decision: reject; the extra helper and duplicated routing made every target 15 to 18 percent slower

candidates.name: success proof in existing isolated K2 terminal
candidates.decision: reject; even without an added public helper the proof is 1.4 to 3.8 percent slower and cannot meet the five-percent promotion gate

correctness_and_review.independent_static_review: The fast predicate's true result proves the same successful CheckScratch and ValidateK2R1EncodeBuffers conditions for the exact native-GF8 cells, uses overflow-checked integer half-open ranges, preserves allowed read-only aliases, and falls back for every ambiguous or invalid input.
correctness_and_review.qualification_boundary: The candidates were killed by the target timing screen. Broad invalid-input differential, sanitizer, exact-main, and neighboring-cell campaigns were intentionally not run because no candidate approached the same-source promotion threshold.

conclusion: Retain the mature K2/R1 validator. The tiny-call gap to Leopard1 is not closed by duplicating its success proof; further work would need a different API-level amortization strategy rather than more validation branches.
